question: Can a frozen, off-the-shelf LM gain from retrieval by simply prepending retrieved documents to its input, and how should documents be selected for language modeling?
hypothesis: Simple prepending with off-the-shelf retrievers gives large LM gains, and LM-specialised reranking adds more.
contributions: In-Context RALM: prepend a retrieved document to the input of an unmodified LM
Study of off-the-shelf retrievers, retrieval stride and query length
Two reranking methods (zero-shot LM reranking, trained Predictive Reranking)
Application to open-domain QA with frozen LLaMA

method.summary: A retrieved passage (single document) is prepended to the prefix of a frozen LM; retrieval is repeated every s tokens using the last l tokens as the query. BM25 top-16 can be reranked by an LM zero-shot or by a RoBERTa-base reranker trained with LM signal.

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.preprocessing: 120 dev/test articles removed from the retrieval corpus

datasets.name: WikiText-103 train
datasets.preprocessing: prefix sampled, BM25 top-16, LM likelihood of next stride per document

datasets.name: RealNews
datasets.preprocessing: training data used as retrieval corpus

datasets.name: The Pile: ArXiv, Stack Exchange, FreeLaw
datasets.preprocessing: training data used as retrieval corpus

datasets.name: Wikipedia Dec 20 2018 (DPR version)
datasets.size: non-overlapping passages of 100 words (<150 tokens mostly)

models.name: BERT-base mean pooling, Contriever, Spider, DPR

training.objective: -log sum_i p_rank(d_i|x) * p_theta(y|[d_i;x]) with the LM frozen; only the reranker trains

other.note: The LMs themselves are not trained; only the optional reranker is.

inference.prompting: Closed-book: 'Answer these questions: Q: ... A:' (Touvron et al. 2023). Open-book: retrieved passages (title + text) prepended, then 'Based on these texts, answer these questions: Q: ... A:'
inference.retrieval: single document for LM; top-2 DPR docs for ODQA; BM25 query = last l tokens, refreshed every s tokens; passages truncated at 256 tokens

metrics.name: token-level perplexity
metrics.definition: shared vocabulary so comparable across GPT-2 models; RealNews and Pile sets

eval.protocol: Hyperparameters tuned on dev sets; single runs; no significance tests or seeds reported

limits: Only a single document is prepended for language modeling; multi-document left to future work.
Retrieval every s tokens costs runtime; the paper does not time it and suggests adaptive retrieval as future work.
Main metric is perplexity; ODQA is a small controlled check.
Predictive reranker needs in-domain training data and was trained on WikiText-103 only; its gap to the top-16 oracle remains.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; models max sequence length fixed at 1,024.
Gains shrink at larger LLaMA sizes (33B: 6.3 to 6.1).

terms.definition: concatenating the retrieved documents within the Transformer’s input prior to the prefix, without altering the LM weights
s, the number of tokens between consecutive retrieval operations
l, the number of last prefix tokens used as retrieval query

lineage.work: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens (RETRO)
lineage.note: closest prior work; needs architecture change and training; couples s and l
concurrent prepending work with trained retriever
Wikipedia corpus, DPR retriever for ODQA
reranking framework similar to zero-shot LM reranking
